reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about configurational entropy, diffusion barriers, and the effects of quenching versus annealing, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific behavior of multi-element nanoparticles under these conditions, so the lack of cited support leaves all key premises ungrounded.
premises: High configurational entropy in near-equiatomic multi-element nanoparticles minimizes atomic diffusion and segregation
Rapid quenching locks in high configurational entropy, creating a large free-energy barrier against phase separation
Annealing reduces the entropy advantage, enabling diffusion-driven segregation and coarsening
Entropy stabilization maintains uniform solid-solution under high-temperature service conditions (773–1923 K)
Retention of high configurational entropy leads to superior catalytic and thermoelectric performance
